talk: From Agents to Scale: Engineering AI Infrastructure on GKE
description:
As AI agents and inference workloads continued to evolve, the session explored how Kubernetes infrastructure had adapted to meet the growing demands of modern AI applications.

The talk examined how Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) enabled the development of scalable AI infrastructure through secure, isolated execution environments for agents, faster workload initialization, dynamic resource adjustments, and hardware-aware scheduling. It also highlighted how intelligent inference traffic routing helped optimize model-serving workloads.

By bringing together innovations across agent execution, compute orchestration, and networking, the session demonstrated how Kubernetes capabilities could be combined to build more flexible, efficient, and scalable infrastructure for AI workloads.

talk: Engineering the Future of Kubernetes with AI
description:
The rapid adoption of AI agents and large-scale model inference is introducing new infrastructure challenges that traditional Kubernetes architectures were not designed to address alone. Workloads now require stronger isolation, faster provisioning, flexible resource management, specialized hardware access, and more sophisticated traffic distribution.

This talk explores the capabilities of Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) that address these emerging requirements. We look at how agent workloads can run in isolated execution environments, how workload startup can be accelerated, how compute resources can be adjusted dynamically, and how hardware-aware scheduling and intelligent inference routing improve overall infrastructure efficiency.

By examining innovations across the execution, compute, and networking layers, this session demonstrates how Kubernetes can serve as a foundation for operating modern AI platforms with greater flexibility, performance, and scalability.

talk: Building AI Infrastructure at Scale with Kubernetes on Google Kubernetes Engine
description:
As AI agents and model inference systems continue to evolve, their growing complexity and fluctuating resource demands are pushing Kubernetes beyond the boundaries of traditional container orchestration.

This session examines how Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) provides a foundation for building the next generation of AI infrastructure. We explore secure, isolated environments for agent execution, optimized workload initialization, live resource resizing, accelerator-aware scheduling, and intelligent inference request distribution.

Through a unified view of the agent, compute, and networking layers, we present practical architectural approaches for creating more efficient, responsive, and adaptable Kubernetes platforms capable of supporting AI workloads at scale.

talk: Orchestrating Intelligence Behind the Scenes
description:
Delivered at Jetisu Digital Forum DevFest Taldykorgan 2026, this session explored the systems engineering powering high-scale AI and machine learning workloads on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).

The talk examined intelligent workload orchestration and autoscaling across GPUs and TPUs, high-throughput networking, and LLM inference stacks (including Gemini, Gemma, and vLLM), showing how Kubernetes and accelerated cloud infrastructure combine to deliver scalable, cost-efficient AI platforms.

event: 1st National AI in Surgery Congress (1. Ulusal Yapay Zeka Cerrahi Kongresi)
talk: Transforming Surgical Problems into AI Projects with Google AI Agents Workshop
description:
Transforming Surgical Problems into AI Projects with Google AI Agents Workshop.

The workshop focuses on moving beyond using artificial intelligence merely as a conversational Q&A tool, demonstrating how clinical workflow challenges and surgical research questions can be formulated into production-ready, agentic AI projects.

Session Agenda (60 Minutes):
1. Framing Surgical Problems as AI Problems: Scoping and decomposing clinical research challenges into modular, AI-addressable components.
2. Live Agentic AI Workflow: Exploring multi-agent orchestration without code—watching an orchestrator agent collaborate with specialized sub-agents handling literature/evidence discovery, clinical guideline retrieval, and evidence synthesis to contrast basic single-prompt chatbots with multi-step agentic systems.
3. Live Surgical Research Case Study: Working through an actual surgical inquiry, demonstrating problem decomposition, automated literature exploration, knowledge source querying, and evidence consolidation.
4. Hands-on Participant Implementation: Interactive blueprinting on participants' own laptops using a structured design framework (Problem → User → Input → Output → AI Tasks → Tools/Knowledge Sources → Expected Outcomes → Next Steps), leaving clinicians and researchers with actionable, concrete project concepts.
5. Multimodal AI & Computer Vision Demo: Demonstrating how foundation vision models analyze surgical video and imaging data, integrating visual modalities into surgical intelligence workflows.

event: 1st National AI in Surgery Congress (1. Ulusal Yapay Zeka Cerrahi Kongresi)
talk: The Next Era of AI in Healthcare
description:
As part of the First National Congress on Artificial Intelligence in Surgery (UYZCK 2026), the keynote session The Next Era of AI in Healthcare explored the evolving role of artificial intelligence in healthcare and its potential to transform clinical practice, medical research, and surgical workflows.

The session highlighted Google's healthcare AI initiatives and research, including Gemini, Google DeepMind's work in health, AMIE, and MedGemma. It also introduced key Google Cloud capabilities, including Vertex AI and agentic AI technologies, demonstrating how these tools can support the development of intelligent applications, clinical decision-support systems, medical research workflows, and next-generation healthcare solutions.

The session emphasized practical opportunities for healthcare professionals to use Google's AI ecosystem to explore new ideas and translate clinical challenges into technology-enabled solutions.

talk: Kubernetes for AI
description:
Architecting and scaling Kubernetes infrastructure on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) for modern AI agents and large-scale model inference workloads.

Covers isolated agent execution with Agent Sandbox, hardware-aware GPU/TPU scheduling via Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA), fast pod startup, and intelligent LLM traffic routing with GKE Inference Gateway and vLLM.

talk: Building Google Agent Development Kit Agents Workshop
description:
Hands-on developer workshop at Build with AI Alexandria focused on designing, testing, and shipping intelligent AI agents using Google's open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK), Google AI Studio, and Gemini models.

Participants scaffolded Python agent projects, practiced structured system instructions and tool calling, inspected multi-turn execution traces locally, and deployed containerized agent endpoints to Google Cloud.

talk: From Cloud to Code: Navigating Google’s 2026 AI and Platform Innovations
description:
Keynote synthesizing the highest-impact engineering releases from Google Cloud Next and Google I/O into practical architecture guidance for software and platform teams.

Unpacks Gemini and open Gemma model advancements, standardized agent interoperability via Model Context Protocol (MCP), Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), AI Studio developer workflows, and GKE platform upgrades.

talk: Build with AI: Architecting Intelligent Systems
description:
Opening keynote and hands-on technical architecture mentoring at the two-day hybrid Build with AI Prishtina Hackathon hosted at Gjirafa.

Guided developers, students, and startup teams on designing tool-using AI agents with Google ADK, integrating Gemini APIs cleanly, and shipping working cloud prototypes for the final demo showcase.

talk: Building Google Agent Development Kit Agents with Skills and Tools Workshop
description:
Hands-on engineering workshop dedicated to building production-ready AI agents with Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) in Python.

Participants practiced modular skill loading, deterministic tool functions, Model Context Protocol (MCP) server integrations, and local trace debugging to improve multi-step agent reliability and capability.

talk: Build With AI Workshop: Google ADK, Skills, and MCP
description:
Step-by-step hands-on Build with AI workshop centered on constructing modular AI agents using Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), reusable skills, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool servers such as Google Maps Platform.

Attendees worked with Gemini and open Gemma models, Gemini CLI, and Google AI Studio to build a complete agent project and deploy it to Google Cloud.

talk: SRE at Global Scale at Google
description:
Technical talk on Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practices for operating resilient, low-latency distributed systems at global scale on Google Cloud.

Explores actionable SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets, multi-region fault tolerance, observability across infrastructure and application layers, and security-conscious operational automation.

talk: Running AI Agents on Google Cloud with Google ADK Workshop
description:
Hands-on workshop covering the full lifecycle of designing, building, and running autonomous AI agents on Google Cloud using Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) and Gemini LLMs.

Participants implemented tool-augmented agents in practical lab exercises, wired external APIs, containerized the services, and deployed scalable serverless endpoints to Cloud Run.

talk: Building Intelligent Agents and ADK
description:
Conference session at DevFest Bursa exploring how to design, structure, and deploy production-ready autonomous agents using Google's open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK) and Gemini models.

Covers agentic reasoning loops, tool orchestration, context and memory management, and architectural patterns for running reliable ADK services on Google Cloud.

talk: AI Agents and ADK
description:
Technical talk unpacking agentic AI workflows with Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) and the Gemini platform.

Examines short- and long-term memory structures, deterministic tool calling, multi-agent delegation, and evaluation guardrails for moving LLM applications from prototype to production.

talk: Building and Deploying AI Agents with Vertex AI
description:
End-to-end engineering walkthrough of building, evaluating, and deploying intelligent AI agents on Google Cloud Vertex AI.

Covers Vertex AI Agent Engine, Google ADK integration, enterprise data grounding, tool-call observability, and best practices for operating scalable agent workloads in production.

talk: AI Agents and Vertex AI
description:
Technical session at DevFest Kashkadarya (GDG Karshi) on leveraging Google Cloud Vertex AI, Gemini models, and Google ADK to build reliable multi-step AI agents.

Demonstrates how structured instructions, grounded knowledge sources, and typed tool integrations turn single-prompt prototypes into maintainable cloud-native applications.

talk: AI Agents and GKE

Covers Kubernetes pod isolation, accelerator-backed node pools, autoscaling bursty agent traffic, and connecting ADK services with managed Vertex AI and Gemini APIs.

talk: MLOps with GKE
description:

Explores reproducible training pipelines, multi-team GPU scheduling, CI/CD/CT model promotion, and high-availability model serving architectures for production machine learning teams.

talk: End-to-End AI Agent Architectures
description:

Traces the full stack from prompt orchestration, RAG grounding, and ADK tool boundaries through containerized serving, observability, and cost/latency guardrails on Cloud Run and GKE.

talk: Developing Generative AI Applications with Vertex AI Workshop
description:

Combined conceptual sessions and guided labs using multimodal Gemini models, open Gemma models, and agent workflows to customize, evaluate, and deploy production-ready AI applications.

talk: Building AI Agents

Walks through tool calling, grounding with external APIs, serverless container deployment, and practical ways to avoid common agent failure modes in production.

description:

description:
Interactive Google Cloud Study Jam at Piri Reis University guiding students through foundational cloud engineering labs.

Covered provisioning workloads across GKE, Cloud Run, and App Engine, along with cloud networking and security fundamentals.

talk: Serverless App Development with Google Cloud

Demonstrated containerized microservices on Cloud Run, managed PaaS deployments on App Engine, and how serverless services integrate with GKE clusters.

talk: The Role of Technology in Enhancing the Safety of Children and Communities

talk: A New Era for Kubernetes: Google Kubernetes Engine Enterprise

Technical session at DevFest Kocaeli 2023 on architecting and operating secure, reliable multi-cluster Kubernetes platforms with GKE and GKE Enterprise.

Shared production best practices covering cluster security, performance tuning, fleet-wide policy governance, and lessons learned from real-world deployments.

talk: Introduction to Best Practices for Google Kubernetes Engine and GKE Autopilot

Explored how GKE Autopilot automates node provisioning, workload rightsizing, and security hardening while keeping Kubernetes workloads portable and cost-efficient.

talk: Opportunities and Trends with Generative AI
description:
Session at Digital Bridge 2023 in Astana analyzing enterprise generative AI trends, multimodal model adoption, and practical integration paths on Google Cloud.

Highlighted Vertex AI, Gemini, and Cloud AI building blocks for turning generative models into reliable business and developer applications.

talk: Unraveling the Mystery Behind Kubernetes Scheduling
description:

Walked through scheduling queues, filtering and scoring plugins, node affinity and anti-affinity, taints and tolerations, topology spread constraints, and cluster bin-packing optimization.

Compared Compute Engine, App Engine, and Cloud Functions to show how to choose and architect the right compute layer for different application workloads.

talk: Serverless Development with Google Cloud Workshop

Evaluated serverless trade-offs for software teams and concluded with a live App Engine demo covering traffic splitting and zero-downtime version management.

talk: Managing Applications on Google Cloud Workshop

Explored auto-scaling, load balancing, container orchestration, and event-driven serverless patterns, concluding with a hands-on lab deploying and managing live applications on App Engine.
